events.what: Malliaris's expository paper 'On ultrafilter construction' states Theorem 14.1 from a Malliaris-Shelah book manuscript in progress: a 'canonical Boolean algebra' attached to a theory satisfies a strong chain condition for the random graph, extending to simple theories with trivial forking
Malliaris-Shelah, 'Some simple theories from a Boolean algebra point of view' (arXiv:2108.05314)

judgement.doubts: Theorem 14.1 is a technical chain-condition result about a new construction; the record does not say it places any theory in Keisler's order, separates or identifies any class, or bounds anything about the order's structure. That is machinery for the programme (scope none), not a case or a bound. Its proof is only in an unavailable manuscript. The pre-snapshot results (infinitely many classes, continuum many classes, 2021 Boolean-algebra paper) are partial results on a problem still open, so the status is open, not open_stale. If the manuscript later shows the canonical algebra classifying some theories in the order, that would be a case (partial).

corrections.why: F3: the only post-snapshot event is Theorem 14.1 in arXiv:2509.14068, which the record itself calls 'a technical building-block result' and 'a chain-condition lemma' about a new construction. It moves no quantity and settles no restriction of the structure of Keisler's order, so its scope is none and it cannot set the status. Earlier results predate the snapshot and are partial, so the status is open, not open_stale.

other: once Theorem 14.1 is scoped none, the record contains no post-snapshot event that settles or bounds anything on this bullet. This is the alternative the record's competing_reading already argued for.
